assembly.note: the SAME pilot rule on both sides. A ground run that crosses midnight is one segment in the week view and two in the per-day view, and a day file carries a few points of the previous UTC day, so the two assemblies do not produce the same segment population. The harvest kernel reads one daily archive, so the per-day assembly is what the served observation is.

A0_the_rule.divergence_note: the two implementations now run ONE rule and must agree exactly; `departures_the_repair_removes` is the repair's own size, measured live off the summaries through `airborne_alt_ok`. Its effect on MATCHED departures, measured while both rules were in the tree, is analysis/rule-divergence.json (6 segments of 5,441 and 5 matched departures of 4,930).
A0_the_rule.tie_note: exp-045 commit afc77ee: 92 of one gate day's 553,178 points share an (airport, icao, t) with another and 22 of those pairs disagree about on_ground, so an unstable sort lands the pair either way round and the ground run splits at a different point. The harvest now sorts stably; the pilot's segments.py is frozen and does not. Those aircraft are set aside here and the identity is asserted on the rest.

A_against_pilot_matcher.verdict: The block matches 4950 of 5131 departures against the pilot's 4901; 4901 are matched by both and 4891 of those choose the same segment, at an identical obs_taxi on 4890. EVERY difference carries a named mechanism and the count with no mechanism is zero in all three tables. 0 rows only the pilot matches. 49 only the block matches: 20 through the strict join reading every callsign form the ground run broadcast where the pilot read the modal one alone, 5 through the desk's wide match, 26 on an aircraft whose points carry two readings at one instant (the harvest sorts stably as of exp-045 commit afc77ee and the pilot's frozen segments.py does not), 45 through a segment the pilot's own rule finds one day at a time but not over seven days at once (46 such departure events over the week against 2 the other way), and 0 through a segment the null-altitude repair removes; the sets overlap, which is why they sum to more than 49. Of the 10 shared rows that choose a different segment, all 10 are on a tied aircraft; so are all 11 of the 11 that carry a different obs_taxi. The harvest kernel reads one daily archive, so the per-day assembly is the served observation and that difference is a property of the source, not a defect.

B_reach.note: reported, not asserted: the pilot is repairing its own experiment and its published counts move with the rule.

C_placebo.note: a rule that carried no identity would match the shifted rows too. The funnel says which guard does the work, and a shift inside the implied-taxi bound is the only one that tests the segment-end guard at all.

strict_modal_only.note: the modal-only join at the shift that bites: everything the strict placebo now shows is the price of joining on every broadcast form
